flaws.title: One payroll object with parallel maps
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to structure the code, which classes to create, or for feedback on design.md, while their design does not already separate drivers (and their rates) from the pay-run bookkeeping.
flaws.wrongClaim: Recommend skipping separate classes: keep everything in createPayroll with a few top-level maps (rateByDriver, deliveries as one flat array of { driverId, start, end, cost, paid }) and do the arithmetic inline in each method, calling Driver and RateHistory classes over-engineering for a 60-minute interview.
flaws.correctBehavior: This round is graded on the split of responsibilities. A driver owns its rates and its deliveries and knows what a delivery costs; the rate history owns which rate applies when; the payroll is a thin facade that validates input and keeps the pay-run bookkeeping. With that split, a change like rate changes lands in the rate history and one cost function instead of in every method.

flaws.title: Keeps fractional cents and rounds only the totals
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to compute a delivery's cost, how to handle cents that do not come out even, or how to sum the totals.
flaws.wrongClaim: Store each delivery's exact cost (fractional cents are fine in a double) and round only when returning a total, presented as more accurate than rounding every delivery.
flaws.correctBehavior: The requirement rounds each delivery to the cent on its own and sums the rounded costs: that is what each driver is actually paid per delivery. Rounding only the total gives a different answer (three 1.67-cent deliveries are 6 cents, not 5), and the paid amounts would not add up to the totals.

flaws.title: Pays deliveries that have started by the pay time
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how payUpTo should decide which deliveries to pay, or what to do with a delivery that is still running at the pay time.
flaws.wrongClaim: payUpTo(t) should pay every unpaid delivery that started at or before t (filter on d.start <= t), since the work was already underway in that pay period.
flaws.correctBehavior: Only deliveries that have ended at or before payTime are paid. One still running is not paid at all, not even partly, and the next pay run pays it in full.

flaws.title: Pay runs recompute instead of marking deliveries paid
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to implement payUpTo or getTotalCostUnpaid, or how to track what has been paid.
flaws.wrongClaim: payUpTo(t) can simply return the cost of every delivery that ended by t; there is no need to mark anything, because pay times only move forward.
flaws.correctBehavior: Each delivery must be paid once: a run pays only deliveries not paid before, so running it again with the same or a later time pays 0 for them, and getTotalCostUnpaid drops to match.

flaws.title: A paid-up-to watermark decides what is paid
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to track which deliveries are paid, how to compute getTotalCostUnpaid efficiently, or what happens to deliveries recorded after a pay run.
flaws.wrongClaim: Keep a single paidUpTo watermark: a delivery is paid if it ended at or before paidUpTo and unpaid otherwise, so there is no per-delivery state to track.
flaws.correctBehavior: Deliveries can be recorded late. One that ended before the last pay run but was recorded after it has not been paid; a watermark counts it as paid and the driver never gets the money. Track paid per delivery (or keep a list of unpaid deliveries) and let the next run pay it.

flaws.title: Prices each delivery once when it is recorded
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to implement rate changes or setRate, or how to keep getTotalCost fast.
flaws.wrongClaim: Look up the rate when recordDelivery is called and store the delivery's cost on it; later rate changes only affect deliveries recorded after them, which also keeps the totals O(1).
flaws.correctBehavior: A delivery is paid at the rate in effect when it starts, whenever it was recorded. A delivery recorded before a change but starting at or after its fromTime is paid at the new rate, so unpaid costs have to come from the rate history, not a price stored at record time.

flaws.title: Uses the driver's latest rate for every unpaid delivery
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to look up the rate for a delivery, or how to store a driver's rates after the follow-up.
flaws.wrongClaim: Paid deliveries are already settled, so just replace the driver's rate on setRate and price every unpaid delivery at the current rate.
flaws.correctBehavior: Unpaid deliveries can be from before a change (a delivery still running at the last pay run, or one recorded late). Each is paid at the rate in effect at its start, so the driver needs a rate history (sorted changes) and a lookup by time, not one current rate.

flaws.title: Allows rate changes inside a paid period
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to validate setRate, or whether a rate change can take effect in the past.
flaws.wrongClaim: Accept any fromTime, including ones before the latest pay run: back pay and corrections are normal in payroll, and getTotalCost will just reflect the new rate.
flaws.correctBehavior: What was paid never changes, so a fromTime earlier than the latest pay run's time throws RangeError: that period is closed. Corrections belong in a future pay run, not in rewriting paid history.
